title: Model Aliases and Routing — teach sonnet, never hardcoded IDs

questions.prompt: A CI script hardcodes `claude-sonnet-4-5`. A newer Sonnet ships, and on one provider the old id no longer resolves the way the script expects. What is the durable fix?
options: Pin a different old version that still works today
Replace the id with the `sonnet` alias
Delete all model selection and rely on the account default
Wrap the failing request in a retry loop
questions.explanation: The alias is a promise about a job, so it keeps working when the version behind it changes. Pinning a different old version just moves the expiry date. Dropping selection loses the chosen tier. Retries do not help when the id itself is rejected — the request fails the same way twice.

questions.prompt: Mid-session, on a long conversation, you run `/model opus`. The next turn is much slower and more expensive, though you changed nothing else. Why?
options: Opus is simply a slower model for every request
The new model has no cache for this conversation, so the whole history is reprocessed
Switching uploads the conversation a second time
questions.explanation: Each model keeps its own cache, and a switch is a model change, so the next request matches no cached prefix and pays for the entire conversation again. 'Opus is slower' is tempting but wrong here — the change is a one-off recompute, not a permanently slower tier. A rate limit would be an error, not a slow turn.

questions.prompt: You must reproduce a benchmark exactly, next month, on a provider of your choosing. Alias or full model name?
options: The `sonnet` alias, because it always points to the same model
The full model name, with a written reason
Whichever is cheapest on the day of the run
questions.explanation: Reproduction needs the exact version, so you name it in full and record why it is pinned. The alias is the tempting wrong answer because it feels stable — but it is designed to move, which is exactly what you do not want in a benchmark.

questions.prompt: The `sonnet` alias resolves to a newer version on your machine than on a colleague's. What does that tell you?
options: Your alias is misconfigured and needs fixing
The alias resolves per provider, and a specific version is still reachable by its full name
Sonnet is unavailable on your colleague's provider
Aliases are unsafe and should never be used
questions.explanation: Resolution is per provider by design, so different versions are the expected behaviour. Calling it a misconfiguration is the tempting mistake: nothing is broken. 'Unavailable' is wrong too — an earlier Sonnet is still a Sonnet, and pinning the exact one by full name is always available when you need it.
